dedupe_keys.name: london spatial survival model of fire brigade response times and the 2014 station closures

description: This case study models how long the London Fire Brigade takes to reach reported dwelling fires and what the 2014 fire station closures did to those times. The authors, statisticians at Lancaster University, applied spatial survival analysis, a parametric proportional hazards model with harmonic terms for time of day and spatially correlated frailties on an auxiliary grid, to London Fire Brigade response time data, and posted the work as a preprint on arXiv. Coverage is Greater London at fine spatial resolution. The preprint is free to read online on arXiv; the underlying incident data are published by the brigade as open downloads. Caveats: the analysis covers dwelling fires only and the short-term period after the closures, and the preprint has not been peer reviewed. The study showed that the spatial model captures time-of-day and local variation better than descriptive analyses, and identified areas around the closed Belsize, Downham, Kingsland, Knightsbridge, Silvertown, Southwark, Westminster and Woolwich stations where fire cover may be of concern, suggesting logistical limits to keeping response times down. Simulation uses: response time distributions and spatial effects for fire station location and closure scenario models. Related records: the London Fire Brigade incident records (data-london-fire-brigade-incident-records) provide the incident data, and the Victoria fire station study (case_study-victoria-minnesota-fire-station-location-planning) adds a station.
